evaluations.note: 30 on the reference machine since the HPO data hold the free energy and the Cauchy stress (2026-10-01; 16 before). BFGS reaches the upper bound RCUT2B = 6.0 at eval 9 (the best, 1.015561e-01), takes the one-sided gradient there (evals 11-12), and from eval 13 its line search re-evaluates the clamped bound until MAXEVAL = 30 (status COMPLETED, 'MAXEVAL=30 reached'); example 01, the same search with the other cohesive-energy script, ends after 16. Whether BFGS's line search accepts a re-evaluation of the clamped bound depends on the sign of the ~1e-13 relative re-evaluation noise of the warm-started lattice relaxation, so the count is not pinned (evals_tol 14: 16..30, MAXEVAL being 30, see tolerance_rationale); best loss, components and RCUT2B do not depend on it.

tolerance_rationale: Best loss, components and RCUT2B are pinned at the default tolerances. The evaluation count is not deterministic across machines: the optimum is on the clamped bound RCUT2B = 6.0 (eval 9), and whether DLIB:BFGS's line search accepts a re-evaluation there depends on the sign of a ~1e-13 relative, rounding-level drift of the warm-started lattice relaxation. The run stops after 16 evaluations on the reference machine (with exact neighbour lists, 2026-09-30; 17 before) or runs to MAXEVAL = 30 (as example 01 does with the same search), and a 1-ulp change of the hot_a0 start or of one training energy flips it; evals_tol 14 accepts 2..30.
